title: A use case's own fields — software-analysis capability
description: The front matter of one use case, a file `UC-NNN-<slug>.md` in `use-case-model/use-cases/` under the analysis location, optionally in a folder per functional area (software-analysis DEC-001 points 1 to 3): one actor's goal and how the system fulfils it. The body says when it starts, the main path in numbered steps, the variants lettered after the step they branch from, and when it is done; steps and variants are append-only, since journeys and evidence cite them. These are the use case's own fields: its friction block sits in the methodology's container beside them and is the core's (COR-050, COR-053 point 10). A use case anchors to its actor and to each other actor it involves, as artefact anchors, and to the code it exercises and the decisions it relies on: those it rests on and those that answer it. It anchors each architecture view that realises it too (DEC-001 points 4 and 11); the capability's check requires each actor anchor. Applied by `pkit software-analysis validate`; unknown fields are refused.

title.description: The use case's title — its goal in a few words. The body's heading repeats it after the id, `# UC-NNN — <title>`, and the capability's check requires the two to match, so a reader of the front matter alone sees the title the page shows. It may change; the id does not.

actor.description: The actor whose goal this is, by id.

other-actors.description: Each other actor who takes part in the use case, by id: an actor of the analysis, never the use case's own `actor`. The body's *Other actors* says what the use case must protect for each. The capability's check resolves each to an actor and requires it among the use case's artefact anchors, so a changed actor flags every use case it takes part in (DEC-001 point 4). Absent, or empty, where no other actor takes part.
